_comment: The Phase 7 accuracy gate's fixture: >=50 (state, question) pairs spanning all
three question types and the option counts that map onto the temperature
PAIRS NOT PROMPTS: each pair is a full (state, question) so the reference's
top-2 gap can be measured PER PAIR and the pairs stratified by it.
The first version of this fixture measured a reference top-2 gap of at most
0.043 across all 60 pairs -- no pair came close to the plan's 0.20 'decided'
threshold. The cause was THIS fixture, not the model: every choice option was
the instruction text with a different level word in front of it ('routine: what
is the clinical urgency of the presentation'), so the option markers differed by
one token and carried almost no signal. Choice options are now distinct option
CONTENT, which is what a choice question actually is.
Option counts stay uneven on purpose: temp_bucket keys on the option COUNT, so
a fixture with one option count would not exercise the bucket map at all.
states: Right lower lobe consolidation on chest radiograph. Fever 39.2 C. Productive cough for three days. Intravenous antibiotics started. CRP 184 mg/L, WBC 17.2 x10^9/L. Oxygen saturations 92% on room air.
No consolidation on chest radiograph. Heart failure with reduced ejection fraction at 25%. Peripheral oedema to the knees. BNP 1840 pg/mL. Dyspnoea on minimal exertion.
Post-operative day 3 after laparoscopic cholecystectomy. Warm surgical site without erythema or discharge. Afebrile at 37.1 C. WBC 7.8 x10^9/L. Pain well controlled on paracetamol only.
Left-sided pyelonephritis. Flank pain and rigors. Urine culture positive for Escherichia coli. Intravenous gentamicin started. Creatinine rose from 88 to 141 umol/L.
Widespread atopic dermatitis affecting both flexures. Pruritus preventing sleep. No fever, no mucosal involvement, no skin infection. Sleep fragmented and behaviour withdrawn at school.
Acute pulmonary embolism confirmed on CT pulmonary angiogram. Tachycardic at 118 bpm. Right calf swelling. Wells score 8.5. Commenced on therapeutic low molecular weight heparin.
